children: Indian Railways targets June 2027 for the 24-coach sleeper train, with ICF tasked with manufacturing 50 trainsets featuring a pantry car and upgraded passenger facilities

Indian Railways is working towards a June 2027 rollout of its 24-coach Vande Bharat sleeper trains, with the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Chennai responsible for manufacturing 50 trainsets. The proposed configuration incorporates a pantry car, additional toilets, and interior modifications to improve facilities for overnight passengers, as per a media report.

The 24-coach configuration differs from the 16-coach sleeper prototype through the inclusion of a pantry car, which will enable food to be heated and served onboard. ICF is also evaluating interior modifications, while the number of toilets is expected to increase.

Indian Railways plans to introduce more than 200 Vande Bharat sleeper trains in the coming years. Alongside ICF's proposed 50 trainsets, Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML), with support from ICF, is manufacturing 10 trainsets. The Indo-Russian joint venture Kinet has been assigned 120 trainsets, while a consortium of Titagarh and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is responsible for another 80.

The existing 16-coach sleeper prototype comprises 11 air-conditioned three-tier coaches, four air-conditioned two-tier coaches and one air-conditioned First Class coach. The train has a designed operating speed of 160 kmph and a testing speed of 180 kmph. Actual operating speeds will depend on track conditions and the capabilities of individual railway sections.

Passenger amenities include cushioned berths, redesigned access to upper berths, individual reading lights, charging points, refreshment tables and dedicated night lighting. The train also features closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras, an integrated announcement system and visual displays.

The sleeper train incorporates bio-vacuum toilets, including a dedicated accessible toilet for passengers with disabilities. The accessible toilet also includes a baby-care station, while the air-conditioned First Class coach provides a hot-water shower.

Automatic interconnecting doors and sealed gangways are designed to maintain temperature control and cleaner air inside the train. Other systems include a Centralised Coach Monitoring System and an emergency communication facility that allows passengers to contact the driver. Safety and energy-efficiency provisions include KAVACH, the indigenous train anti-collision system, and regenerative braking, which recovers part of the energy generated during braking to improve efficiency.
